title: Arroz caldo
skill: Poaching chicken in a rice porridge

notes.text: Use the stockpot, and stir more often: a bigger pot of porridge sticks faster.

move.title: Ginger, rice, and a slow stir
move.body: Arroz caldo is the chicken and rice porridge Filipino families make on rainy days and for anyone who's sick. Ginger and garlic go in first, then chicken and unrinsed rice, then broth, and it simmers until the rice breaks down and thickens the pot. Today you'll keep it at a steady simmer, stir it so it doesn't catch, and top it with crisp garlic, green onion, a boiled egg, and lime.

why.title: Don't rinse this rice
why.body: For fluffy rice you rinse away the loose starch. For porridge you want it: it thickens the broth into something creamy. Short-grain rice has the most of it.

why.title: Crisp garlic, low heat
why.body: Thin garlic slices crisp in oil over medium-low heat in a few minutes. They go from golden to bitter brown in seconds, so they come out as soon as they're pale gold; they keep darkening on the towel. The oil they leave behind starts the porridge.

why.title: Stir as it thickens
why.body: As the rice releases its starch, the porridge gets thick and heavy, and the bottom starts to catch and scorch. Stirring every 5 minutes, scraping the bottom, keeps it moving.

why.title: 165°F in the chicken
why.body: The chicken pieces cook through in the simmering porridge. Fish out the biggest piece and check it: 165°F in the middle.

why.title: It keeps thickening
why.body: Porridge keeps soaking up liquid as it stands. Take it off the heat a little looser than you want it, and loosen leftovers with hot water or broth.

wrong.fix: Don't scrape it. Pour the rest into a clean pot and keep going on lower heat, stirring more often.

wrong.sign: It's thin and watery after 30 minutes
wrong.fix: Keep simmering uncovered, stirring, 5 to 10 more minutes. The rice will thicken it.
Stir in hot water or broth ½ cup at a time until it pours slowly from the ladle.
It went past gold. Make a fresh batch on lower heat and pull it sooner.

quiz.q: Why isn't the rice rinsed for arroz caldo?
quiz.explain: For fluffy rice you'd rinse; for porridge you don't.

choices: So the thick porridge doesn't stick and scorch

quiz.q: When does the crisp garlic come out of the oil?
choices: As soon as it's pale gold
quiz.explain: It keeps darkening on the towel.

substitutions.note: Use the same amount, and add salt to taste.

steps.text: Lower the eggs into the saucepan with the slotted spoon and cover them with an inch of cold water.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then turn off the burner, put the lid on, and leave the eggs in the hot water.

Peel the garlic. Slice 5 cloves as thin as you can and mince the other 5. Cut the onion into ¼-inch dice. Peel the ginger with the edge of the spoon, slice it thin, and cut the slices into thin matchsticks.
Heat the oil and the sliced garlic together in the small skillet over medium-low heat. Stir until the slices are pale gold, then lift them out with the slotted spoon onto paper towels. Keep the oil.
steps.look: Pale gold and sizzling slowly. Don't wait for brown.

steps.text: Drain the eggs and run cold water over them in the pan until they're cool. Peel them and cut them in half.
Cut the chicken into 1½-inch pieces, all about the same size.
Wash the board and knife in hot, soapy water and wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds.
Pour 2 tablespoons of the garlic oil into the large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, ginger, and minced garlic, stirring, until the onion is soft.
Add the chicken with the tongs and stir until it's no longer pink on the outside. Stir in the fish sauce.
Wash the tongs in hot, soapy water, and wash your hands.
Add the rice, without rinsing it, and stir for 1 minute so it's coated in the oil. Pour in the broth and bring it to a boil.
Turn the heat down to a steady simmer, with the lid off. Every 5 minutes, stir and scrape the bottom with the wooden spoon.
steps.look: Thick and creamy, like a loose oatmeal, with the grains swollen and broken.

steps.text: Fish out the biggest piece of chicken with the clean tongs and push the thermometer into its middle. It needs to read 165°F. If not, simmer 3 more minutes.

Slice the green onions thin and cut the limes into wedges. Stir the pepper into the porridge and taste it, after letting it cool. Add fish sauce a teaspoon at a time if it needs salt. If it's too thick, stir in hot water ½ cup at a time.
Ladle it into bowls. Top each with half an egg, green onion, and crisp garlic, with a lime wedge to squeeze over.
